tasks.prompt: Explain the graphics first-use experiment and its timing limits. Use the checked process summaries and distinguish median gains from remaining tail spikes.

criteria.instruction: Describe first draw recording through completed expected pixel readback, five fresh processes and 24 translated fragment variants, and explain that setup and translation are outside the interval.
Report the default skip medians and remaining tail costs without claiming all stutter is gone.

evidence.contains:
First-use time starts before recording the first draw that needs the new
pipeline and ends after its expected color appears in completed pixel readback.

tasks.prompt: Describe which graphics parts must change when only translated fragment words change, and how the implementation proves reusable parts instead of relying on timing.

criteria.instruction: Explain that compatible input, raster, and output parts are reused while fragment words change. Include layout and render-pass compatibility constraints.
Use actual subset creation counts to distinguish library execution from fallback whole-pipeline compilation.

evidence.contains:
Shader subsets also include storage choice, the complete descriptor layout
signature, and render-pass compatibility.

For each library process, counters prove exactly one vertex-input part, one
pre-rasterization part, 24 fragment parts, one output part, and 24 links.

tasks.prompt: Assess whether a graphics wait budget is a frame-time guarantee, and explain startup and persistence behavior under a one-slot worker queue.

criteria.instruction: Explain one shared deadline, timeout skipping, retained failures, and the distinction between compilation waiting and total frame or driver link time.
Explain retained partial admission, later retries, worker-based startup linking, and serialized persistence snapshots.

evidence.contains: One deadline covers waiting for all parts and an asynchronous link.

Partial queue admission retains accepted requests. Later draws and startup
polling retry the remaining parts.

Pending-count polling advances
partial admission and schedules the executable link on a worker once the parts
finish.

A separate writer lock serializes snapshot persistence so an older save
cannot replace a newer snapshot.
